## TDD Workflow

CARL implementation follows Red → Green → Refactor. Phase 0 creates executable BDD coverage, fixtures, and real-artifact evidence before implementation can be called done. No new non-BDD test files are planned; executable coverage lives in `tests/features/carl-integration.feature`, `tests/step_definitions/feature_carl_integration.ts`, and CARL fixtures.

- [x] Wire Claude Code CARL runtime consumer through plugin hook — id: wire-runtime-consumer — Status: DONE | Est: 90m

  _Changes:_
  - Implement the CARL runner as the runtime consumer that checks manifest consistency, platform support, runtime availability, and real CARL invocation evidence.
  - Register the distributed hook wrapper in `.claude-plugin/hooks.json` so runtime proof uses the plugin-distributed entry path, not a side-channel helper.

  - [ ] Runtime-consumer evidence proves the same `.claude-plugin/hooks.json` command path reaches `tools/carl/runner.ts`.
  - [ ] The hook entry is verified in a deps-absent mode if it imports non-`node:` dependencies, preventing plugin-user dead integration.

## Phase 2: Fail-open warning path (Green)

- [x] Implement fail-open warning injection — id: implement-fail-open-warning — Status: DONE | Est: 60m

  _Changes:_
  - Convert missing dependency, timeout, malformed output, unsupported platform, and runtime exceptions into fail-open hook results.
  - Inject the concise agent-visible warning `CARL did not run; tell the user CARL guidance/recall was unavailable.` through the verified Claude Code hook context mechanism.

  **Done When:**
  - [ ] @feature4 verifies broken CARL runtime dependency exits fail-open and keeps the main agent session continuing.
  - [ ] Agent-visible context contains the required warning and reminder to tell the user that CARL guidance/recall was unavailable.
  - [ ] Successful hook execution does not emit the failure warning.
